items.title: Trump rejects Iran peace proposal, plans renewed bombing after US elections: WSJ
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting within seven days, and told aides he expects to resume bombing after November congressional elections, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing unnamed US officials. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi had told reporters at the United Nations on Friday that Iran conveyed its peace plan to the US through Qatari mediators, saying a deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting. A US official had told Reuters that the US and and Iran were having "positive and constructive discussions through the mediators," but Trump was privately skeptical that Iran that would meet his demands, the Journal report said.

items.title: Traffic policeman hit by car while controlling traffic for Kelantan Sultan’s convoy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 22-year-old traffic policeman was injured after being struck by a car while controlling traffic for the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V’s convoy in Tumpat, Kelantan, yesterday. The incident occurred at about 1.25pm at the Kampung Kepulau traffic-light junction in Palekbang, where the officer from the Tumpat district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division was closing the road from Morak towards Palekbang. According to Harian Metro , Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the road closure was to allow Sultan Muhammad V’s convoy to pass as the Kelantan Ruler travelled to Friday prayers and a public feast held in conjunction with his 57th birthday celebrations.

items.title: Moro Islamic Liberation Front says Malaysia’s role ‘indispensable’ to Philippines’ Bangsamoro peace process
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — After decades of facilitating the Bangsamoro peace process, Malaysia remains an indispensable and trusted ‘honest broker’ whose involvement should continue until the process reaches its conclusion, according to the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF). MILF Peace Implementing Panel chairman Mohagher Iqbal said Malaysia had earned a high level of trust from both the MILF and the Philippine government through its impartiality and record in facilitating negotiations since 2001. “Malaysia’s facilitation is indispensable.

items.title: Malaysia calls for reform of international financial system, multilateral trade
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has called for reforms to international financial institutions and a more effective multilateral trading system for developing countries. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said developing countries needed to play a meaningful role in shaping the future direction of these systems. He said Global South cooperation demonstrated that developing countries were not merely recipients of development solutions, but also strategic partners and contributors to global development.

items.title: Ahead of Budget 2027, Anwar invites small entrepreneurs to identify those needing support
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is allowing small entrepreneurs in every village to propose aid recipients following the government’s plan to increase the specific allocation for the group in Budget 2027. Anwar said many stalls run by small entrepreneurs also provided employment, thereby helping to generate income for the local community. “When we give aid to these small entrepreneurs, even if it is small, they work hard and truly appreciate the assistance given,” he added.

items.title: US networks return to White House pool as Trump media battle rages on
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump's White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Trump last week banned the three outlets from the White House, before a judge ordered the administration to restore their access. The White House television press pool aired video of Xi's arrival at the White House for tea on the final day of the Chinese leader's visit, as well as the two leaders' tour of the National Archives, which houses the US Constitution.

items.title: Pairin Kitingan: Mother tongues risk fading when no longer spoken at home
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Mother tongues risk fading when they are no longer regularly heard and spoken, particularly at home. Kadazandusun Cultural Association president Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan said this is a risk he knew from personal experience. Eventually, I could speak Hakka.

items.title: Anwar approves RM2.8m to repair Islamic education institutions in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional allocation of RM2.8 million this year to repair basic infrastructure at 14 Islamic education institutions across Kedah. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the allocation was to ensure students could study in a more comfortable and safe environment. In the same post, Anwar also announced a RM250,000 allocation to implement hadith-related programmes.

items.title: Form Two student dies after being found unconscious at Kuala Pilah school hostel, bullying alleged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 14-year-old Form Two student died last night after being found unconscious at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, amid allegations from his family that he had been bullied. Kuala Pilah district police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin confirmed the incident and said further details would be released soon, the New Straits Times reported. According to the report, the student was found unconscious at the hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.

items.title: Anwar: China trip boosts investment prospects and trade ties for both nations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described his recent working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou as yielding significant results, particularly in harnessing investment potential and trade cooperation that will generate widespread benefits and prosperity for both Malaysia and China. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, stated that both countries must leverage their diplomatic relations — currently at an all-time high — to continue exploring opportunities and pioneering new, highly promising collaborations. He noted that Malaysia’s participation in the WorldSkills Competition and Summit, as well as the Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE), has showcased the nation’s capabilities on the international stage.

items.title: TikTok pays Alabama US$100m to avoid trial over teen safety
items.summary: WASHINGTON: TikTok on Friday agreed to pay Alabama at least US$100 million and enact limits for teen users, avoiding a trial set to begin next week in the southern US state over claims related to child safety on the platform. "Under the settlement, Alabama will receive a minimum of US$100 million, due to the state within 45 days, with the potential to receive up to US$300 million if certain conditions are met," the office of the Attorney General Steve Marshall said. According to Marshall, TikTok has agreed to enact two-hour daily time limits and restrict access for children from midnight to 6am, among a host of other parental and other safety features.

items.title: Elderly woman loses RM80k in 'ghost money aid' scam
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 73-year-old woman lost RM80,000 after falling victim to a scam offering fake "ghost money aid". He said the incident began last year when the victim, who was at home, became interested in obtaining "ghost money aid" advertised online through Facebook. Azli said the person later informed the victim that the money had been deposited into her account.

items.title: Anwar firm on non‑interference, says Negeri Sembilan ruler’s position must be decided under Constitution
items.summary: He said under the constitutional monarchy system practised in the country, any action concerning a Ruler could not be taken arbitrarily but must be based on constitutional provisions. “I said I am not interfering. Anwar said issues involving the Ruler should not be taken lightly as Malaysia practises a constitutional monarchy that places the royal institution within the framework of the Constitution.

items.title: Elderly fisherman's body found on Melaka beach
items.summary: MELAKA: The body of an elderly fisherman was found lying face down along the beach near Jalan Residen, Padang Temu, here yesterday. He said a man reported finding the body near the beach opposite 8 Residence, Jalan Residen, Taman Padang Temu. "Police found the victim, a 74-year-old man identified as Mohammad Chalip.

items.title: Anwar denies trying to interfere in Negri Sembilan royal crisis
items.summary: PENDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied trying to interfere in the Negri Sembilan royal crisis. He said he was defending the constitutional monarchy system practised in the country. Anwar said he did not want action by the Undangs in the state to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar too easily, as this could lead to a wider crisis for the constitutional monarchy system.

items.title: Student death prompts calls for transparent probe, stern action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah has prompted calls for a thorough investigation into alleged bullying. The student was found unconscious at the school hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead. Former Education Minister Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin, in a post on Threads, conveyed his condolences to the student's family and urged the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation without compromise.

items.title: Weak 3.3-magnitude earthquake strikes Sabah’s Kuamut, no tsunami threat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.3 in magnitude was detected in the Kuamut area of Kinabatangan, Sabah, at 5.32am today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake was centred at 5.1 degrees north and 116.8 degrees east, at a depth of 118km. MetMalaysia said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

items.title: Serian records unhealthy API reading
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Serian recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 154 as of 7am today. In Sabah, the monitoring station at Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded an API reading of 84, while Tawau and Sandakan recorded 78 and 72 respectively. In Johor, Pasir Gudang recorded an API reading of 83, while Larkin recorded 81.

items.title: Form Two student dies after alleged bullying at school hostel
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: A Form Two student at a school in the district died last night, reportedly after being bullied at the school hostel. The 14-year-old was reportedly found unconscious at the school hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead. Meanwhile, Kuala Pilah district police chief, Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin, confirmed the incident and said further details would be provided soon.

items.title: Trump warns Xi against Iran support as Beijing pledges no assistance
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump warned Chinese President Xi Jinping against providing support to Iran during talks in Washington this week and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said on Friday. David Perdue, Trump's ambassador to Beijing, said in a CNBC interview that Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect support for Iran was "totally unacceptable." Asked separately on Fox News if that meant China would stop assisting Iran, Perdue said Washington received assurances from Beijing on Thursday.

items.title: #NSTviral: Storm leaves Klang Valley roads clogged, hawker stalls wrecked
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists faced heavy rain, fallen trees and severe traffic congestion across parts of the Klang Valley yesterday, with several roads blocked by fallen trees. One user, ayranajihabtmuhdherry, said traffic had been reduced to a single lane. The rain wasn't even heavy earlier," the user wrote.

items.title: Beyond bigger pay cheques, what can keep Malaysia's frontline workers from Singapore? [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For Malaysian workers weighing whether to stay in Malaysia or cross the Causeway for a bigger pay cheque, the dilemma goes beyond Singapore's higher salaries. The study found that 39 per cent of Malaysians working in the city-state were skilled workers, 35 per cent semi-skilled and 26 per cent low-skilled. THE CAUSEWAY WAGE GAP Khazanah Research Institute research associate Wan Amirah Wan Usamah said Singapore's higher wages reflected not only productivity but also deliberate policies to raise workers' pay.

items.title: Pentagon wins court battle to exclude Anthropic from AI supply chain
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A US appeals court upheld on Friday the Pentagon's decision to exclude Anthropic from its supply chain, a decision taken when the AI startup refused to remove certain safeguards on its Claude model. The conflict began in February when Anthropic refused Pentagon Secretary Pete Hegseth's demand to remove restrictions on the use of Claude for fully autonomous lethal weapons and mass domestic surveillance of Americans. The supply chain risk designation, formally made in March, canceled Anthropic's military contracts and barred other Pentagon contractors from using its technology.

items.title: Lula bans online sports betting days before Brazil election
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Friday banned sports betting sites, the biggest sponsor of the country's football clubs, just days before a nailbiter election in which he is seeking a fourth term. "It is no longer possible to deposit money into betting sites in the country," said Finance Minister Dario Durigan, announcing the ban at an event alongside Lula. "Brazil spent years debating how to regulate sports betting," the club said in a statement.

items.title: Children caught in porn web, murders among major crimes this week [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of eight children in a police operation, which also uncovered more than 2.1 million child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and pornography files, was among some of the major crimes reported this week. The police operation, codenamed Op Pedo 3.0, exposed the disturbing production and sale of CSAM-related videos and animations through closed online groups for between RM50 and RM60. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC would continue strengthening its technical and forensic cooperation with police to track those misusing network services to sexually exploit children online.

items.title: Rais charged with sedition, Najib back in court after conditional pardon [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim was charged with sedition in relation to the current Negri Sembilan constitutional crisis. Then there was former Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani who was charged with four counts of accepting over RM300,000 in house renovation costs. RAIS CHARGED WITH SEDITION IN RELATION to NEGRI CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS In Melaka, Rais, who is also Parti Wawasan Negara chairman pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court to a charge under the Sedition Act.

items.title: Piranhas in Pahang? What we know about the mystery fish found at Klau Dam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Piranhas are not native to Malaysia. What are piranhas? Piranhas are freshwater fish belonging to the family Serrasalmidae , a group that also includes closely related fish such as pacus.

items.title: Trump took Xi on ballroom tour: White House
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump took Chinese President Xi Jinping and other state dinner guests on a tour of the construction site of his new ballroom, the White House said Friday. Journalists were then led out of the dinner, but a White House official told AFP they "can confirm they took a tour," when asked if Trump had later taken Xi and other guests to see the ballroom. The US president had earlier shown Xi the outside of the ballroom while giving the Chinese president a tour of the new White House helipad, during which he also took Xi aboard his helicopter, Marine One.--AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Trump, Xi summit ends with pomp, pandas and few major breakthroughs
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump took Chinese leader Xi Jinping to see the founding documents of American democracy on Friday, capping a state visit full of pomp and pageantry but with no major breakthroughs. Trump said he discussed the stalled Iran war with Xi, and the two leaders confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the United States. But as Trump showed Xi around the National Archives in Washington – home to the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution – it underscored that the summit was more about spectacle than substance.

items.title: Malaysia calls for Myanmar to fulfil Asean Five-Point Consensus
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has stressed the importance of Myanmar fulfilling its responsibilities as an Asean member and implementing the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) to help address the prolonged crisis in the country. This was among the positions conveyed by Malaysia during a courtesy call by International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) president Mirjana Spoljaric on Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. The two sides also discussed autonomous weapons systems, which are receiving increasing attention from the international community.

items.title: China visit opens new investment, trade opportunities, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou has opened new opportunities for Malaysia to tap investment potential and strengthen trade cooperation with China, bringing shared benefits to the people of both countries. Anwar said the visit also showcased Malaysia's capabilities on the international stage through the country's participation in the WorldSkills Competition and Summit, as well as the Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE). He said dialogue and cooperation must continue to be strengthened amid global competition and uncertainty to build a fairer and more equitable world.

items.title: Traffic policeman injured after car rams him during road closure
items.summary: TUMPAT: A traffic policeman was injured after being hit by a car while controlling traffic at the Kampung Kepulau traffic light intersection in Palekbang yesterday. Tumpat district police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said the 22-year-old policeman from the Tumpat Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division (BSPTD) was closing the road from Morak to Palekbang at about 1.25pm. Mohd Khairi said the case was being investigated under Section 79(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Govt reviewing systems to move business applications fully online, says Hannah
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The government is reviewing processes and systems to fully transition business applications online, allowing entrepreneurs to avoid spending unnecessary time following up with officers on application status. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said unnecessary procedures would be eliminated to ease the administrative burden on businesses, improve time and cost efficiency and reduce room for corruption. Speaking at the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) Installation and 34th Anniversary Night, Hannah said the government must also improve its delivery systems if businesses were expected to adapt and improve.

items.title: Cambodian delegation explores trade, investment ties during Malaysia visit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Cambodian delegation visited Malaysian household convenience store chain KK Super Mart as part of a business engagement aimed at deepening trade and investment ties between the two countries. The delegation was welcomed by the Malaysia-Cambodia Business Association (MCBA) and Malaysia Chinese Assembly Hall (MCAH) on Sept 24, with discussions also covering potential cooperation in education, healthcare, tourism and business. Yaw said MCBA would continue working with MCAH, Soccom and other business associations through business missions, trade exhibitions, investment visits, business matching and people-to-people exchanges.

items.title: Anwar approves RM2.8mil to repair infrastructure at 14 Islamic institutions in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM2.8 million allocation this year to repair basic infrastructure at 14 Islamic education institutions in Kedah. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the allocation was aimed at ensuring students could study in a more comfortable and safe environment. In the same post, Anwar also announced a RM250,000 allocation for hadith-related programmes.

items.title: Saifuddin: Rule of law, good governance must guide Negri Sembilan administration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The principles of the rule of law and good governance must be upheld to ensure all administrative actions are taken within the limits of legal powers and provisions, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the recent suspension of Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal highlighted the importance of ensuring that all administrative actions were based on a clear understanding of the relevant powers and legal provisions. "The Constitutional and State Law Division of the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has affirmed that the Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) has no legal authority to suspend the duties of the two senior officials.

items.title: NST Leader: Policing cyberspace for online sexual predators
items.summary: A Federal Bureau of Investigation probe into Epstein's crimes had amassed three million files, including 180,000 images and 2,000 videos, plus government documents, emails and flight logs. While thankfully not of the same scale as in Epstein's case, the problem is serious enough that 53 people, including eight children, were recently arrested during a nationwide operation targeting child sexual abuse material. Since 2024, 2.1 million files containing child sexual abuse material and pornography have been uncovered.

items.title: Brazil election candidates mount digital armies
items.summary: IN a knife-edge election race, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and main rival Flavio Bolsonaro have deployed volunteer digital armies online to spread their messages and battle for voters. These online campaigns, unprecedented in scale in Brazil, have highlighted the growing role of social media in the country's politics, while also raising questions about compliance with election rules. Lula has launched his own social media initiative dubbed "Lula's Spokespersons", aimed at boosting voter engagement.

items.title: 'A gesture of gratitude': Najib's family thanks public for contributions towards RM50mil fine
items.summary: PEKAN: The family of Datuk Seri Najib Razak has expressed appreciation for public contributions towards paying the RM50 million fine imposed on the former prime minister. Mohamad Nizar, who is also Pekan Umno deputy chief, was speaking at a Pekan Umno press conference following the conditional pardon granted to Najib by the Federal Territories Pardons Board. Also present was Pekan Umno chief Datuk Seri Mohammad Fakhruddin Mohd Arif.

items.title: Kuching Marathon cancellation a blow to 13,000 participants who made travel plans, says Sarawak sports minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — Sarawak Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah has expressed disappointment over the last-minute cancellation of Kuching Marathon 2026, which had attracted more than 13,000 registered participants. He said the decision was particularly difficult for participants from outside Sarawak who had made advance arrangements, including booking flights and accommodation. Meanwhile, KMA said registered participants could collect their finisher medals and finisher tees tomorrow (Sept 26) and Sunday at the Alfresco area of Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre.

items.title: EC: 43,309 new voters added in August — check the electoral roll by October 24
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for August 2026 (DPT BLN8/2026) is open for review for 30 days until Oct 24, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus. Khairul Shahril said it also includes 34,411registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies and 2,728 voters who have changed their voter category or status. “Checks can be made via the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the official state election office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my, the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak mobile application, or the Voter Registration Check hotline at 03-8892 7218,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s Asian Games sepak takraw gold after 36-year wait
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the national men’s sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today. Syabas (Well done) Malaysia. Earlier, the national sepak takraw squad clinched the men’s team regu gold medal after defeating Thailand 2-0 in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Arena.

items.title: Immigration detains 84 foreign nationals in two-phase raid at Putrajaya’s ‘Green Flats’
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department detained 84 foreign nationals under Ops Pintu at Pangsapuri Putra Harmoni, better known as the “Green Flats”, here following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs. It said 60 Immigration personnel conducted the operation in two phases beginning yesterday. It said 321 people were inspected, while 84 foreign nationals — 73 men, nine women and two children — were detained for further investigation.

items.title: Malaysian Bar seeks disclosure of taxpayer cost of Najib house arrest, plans fresh court challenge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Malaysian government should disclose the additional cost to taxpayers if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak serves the remainder of his SRC International jail term under house arrest, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj said today. In a statement, Anand urged the Federal Territories Pardons Board and the Prime Minister’s Department to disclose two things to the public: “Declassify and publish the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting(s) held regarding Najib’s First Pardon and Najib’s Second Pardon decisions”; and “Fully disclose all conditions proposed to be attached to Najib’s house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and the additional costs to taxpayers that a ‘house arrest’ would entail.” Anand also announced today that the Malaysian Bar would go to court to challenge the Pardons Board’s decision and advice concerning Najib’s second pardon.

items.title: EC denies report of 15 new parliamentary seats for Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) has denied a report claiming that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased, saying there is currently no proposal to alter the number of federal seats in the state. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said no documents had been shared indicating that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased to any particular number. The review proposes 17 new state constituencies, increasing the number of Sarawak Legislative Assembly seats from 82 to 99, as well as changes to the names of several existing state constituencies and one parliamentary constituency.

items.title: MACC completes Kedah fertiliser probe, two may face charges soon
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed its investigation into the delayed supply of fertilisers in Kedah, with two individuals set to be charged soon in connection with the case. “The MACC investigation into the issue of fertiliser distribution to farmers and paddy planters in Kedah has been completed. On September 7, the MACC opened an investigation paper into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser, or Paddy Fertiliser 3, to Kedah paddy farmers.

items.title: MACC chief: Two former Felda officials to be charged over Kuala Lumpur Vertical City project next week
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — Two individuals being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project linked to Felda will be charged next week, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said. He said the two were a former Felda general manager and a former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee, also known as Felda Investment Commission. The KLVC investigation is among seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.

items.title: More questioning awaits Isa Samad in Felda probe once he recovers from eye surgery, says MACC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will resume recording the statement of Datuk Seri Isa Samad once the former Felda chairman recovers from a medical procedure. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa is being treated at the Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery. “Regarding Isa’s statement, we had to put it on hold.

items.title: Witness tails fleeing hatchback after attempted theft, helping police make arrest in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — A witness who followed a hatchback believed to have been used by two men fleeing an attempted vehicle component theft helped police trace their movements and arrest one suspect here last night. He said the witness spotted two men allegedly attempting to steal components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop. “A witness noticed two suspicious men trying to steal the components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop before they fled using the hatchback after being confronted.

items.title: MACC to issue asset declaration notices to Saravanan, his wife and three children
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will issue notices to former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan, his wife, and their three children to declare their assets within a month. Its chief commissioner, Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, said that the asset declaration notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009 will be delivered on Monday to Saravanan, his wife, and their two children, while another child who is still abroad will receive it in November. In another development, Abd Halim said his side has not yet received the asset declaration from the former chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, and his family.

items.title: Perak court fines buyer, petrol station owner RM25,000 each over RON95 sale to Singapore car
items.summary: MANJUNG, Sept 25 — An oil palm plantation worker and a petrol station owner were each fined RM25,000 by the Sessions Court here today for their involvement in buying and selling RON95 petrol for foreign-registered vehicles. Wong was charged with violating Regulation 4(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for purchasing 27.452 litres of RON95 petrol for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle. Meanwhile, Ling was charged — at the same date, time, and location — with violating Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for selling the same petrol to Wong for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.

items.title: When will Melaka vote? EC to decide key state election dates on October 7
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on October 7 to discuss matters related to the 16th Melaka state election. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting followed the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly last Wednesday. “The special meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.

items.title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas. In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze. He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.

items.title: PM’s brother Idrus Ibrahim buried in Bukit Mertajam after Friday prayers
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The remains of Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, were laid to rest at the Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Muslim Cemetery here today. The funeral was attended by hundreds of family members, relatives, friends and political leaders from various parties. The prime minister, accompanied by family members and members of the public, walked about 200 metres from the late Idrus’ home to the prayer hall.

items.title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today. The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries, Utusan Malaysia reported. Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.

items.title: Vulnerable groups to be focus of Selangor Budget 2027, says MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Supporting vulnerable groups will be among the Selangor government’s main priorities in Budget 2027, with the aim of ensuring the state’s economic progress benefits people across all segments of society. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor’s development should go beyond strong economic performance and attracting investment to also addressing the needs of groups requiring greater attention, according to a Berita Harian report published today. Amirudin said existing support programmes, including cash handouts and assistance under Bantuan Kehidupan Sejahtera Selangor (Bingkas) and YANIS, would be part of efforts to help vulnerable groups, including those affected by the current energy supply crisis.

items.title: Appeals court lets MAIWP strike out man’s bid to change religion from Islam to Sikhism
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Court of Appeal today allowed appeals by the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and the government to strike out a man’s suit challenging his religious status. The three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid ruled that Shehzad Malik Muhammad Sarwar Malik’s case was a renunciation case and the relief he is seeking could only be granted by the Syariah Court. “The respondent (Shehzad Malik) here cannot come to the Civil Court as the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to grant the orders,” said Justice Mohd Firuz, who delivered the unanimous decision.

items.title: Anwar wraps China visit with RM36.8b in trade, investment pledges
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, is not just a routine diplomatic trip, but rather a new benchmark for the continuation of strategic relations that strengthen cooperation in various fields between the two countries. The working visit at the invitation of the Chinese government not only strengthens bilateral relations, but also opens up new opportunities for Malaysia to expand investments, export markets and cooperation in strategic and high-value economic areas. Summarising the overall outcome of the visit, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the relationship between Malaysia and China is now at a very strong level and is developing positively.

items.title: In Johor, Indonesian teen charged with trafficking over 25kg of illicit drugs
items.summary: The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The offense was also framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The charge was brought under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for illegal possession of drugs and is punishable under Section 39A(1) of the same Act.

items.title: Spell out the offence: Aminudin challenges Negeri MB over royal dispute allegations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution. Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred.
